title: 'We have to keep going' – Mourinho's sights higher than one Clasico win
subtitle: Real Madrid claimed a 2-1 win over LaLiga leaders Barcelona on Sunday, but Jose Mourinho is far from satisfied.
paragraphs: Jose Mourinho is not content with just beating Barcelona as he demanded his Real Madrid team target a title tilt in LaLiga.
Kylian Mbappe's double at Camp Nou propelled Madrid to a  2-1 victory in El Clasico.
Mourinho has now won six Clasicos across his two spells in charge of Los Blancos, with only two Madrid coaches – Miguel Munoz (16) and Carlo Ancelotti (nine) – winning more.
But Mourinho is not satisfied, as he insisted Madrid must now follow up this win.
"This is a great win, but when we get back to work, I'm not going to let anyone have their head in the clouds," Mourinho said.
"Real Madrid don't play to win at Camp Nou, but rather to win the league. We have to keep going.
"I think it was a great game. A game at a high level, a game which the world that loves football stopped to see, and they weren't let down.
"In our case, the boys played an extraordinary game, well organised, focused, with a lot of courage.
"For me it's a great victory for the boys, against a great opponent. The boys deserve it."
Madrid had to do without goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, who was absent due to illness.
Courtois' replacement Andriy Lunin, though, made five saves.
"The only thing I said to Lunin before the game was: you train to play, not to be on the bench," Mourinho added.
"We have the best keeper in the world, but today we weren't crying before the game because Thibaut couldn't play. The group is strong."
